correctness.rationale: For product bodies \(A_i\times B_i\), centroids factor, so the centroid-aligned common-intersection volume is the product of the two factor lazy volumes. For arbitrary independent translations, the intersection itself factors and volume multiplies; maximizing over the translation variables therefore gives the exact product of the two optimal volumes. Hence efficiency multiplies on product instances. Taking near-infimum instances proves \(c_{n+d,m}\le c_{n,m}c_{d,m}\). Subadditivity of \(\log c_{n,m}\) yields the root-limit statement by Fekete, and repeated planar products give the displayed \((4/9)^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}\) upper bound.
